title: Mitigating Routability Problems in Complementary-FET-based VLSI Designs
problem: Complementary FET (CFET) technology at sub-5nm scales stacks P-FET and N-FET for extreme cell area reduction, but reduced standard cell height creates routability challenges: limited pin accessibility and severe routing congestion due to constrained back-end-of-line (BEOL) routing resources.
motivation: CFET enables area scaling but introduces routing bottlenecks; addressing routability is essential for practical deployment of next-generation technology nodes.
method: Framework employs various pin-extended cells on demand to address pin accessibility and routing congestion. Partial placement blockages further alleviate routing congestion through strategic blocking of placement areas.
key_novelty: Pin-extended cells and placement blockages specifically designed to mitigate CFET-specific routability challenges (pin accessibility and BEOL congestion).
contributions: Pin-extended cell library for improved pin accessibility
Placement blockage strategy for routing congestion mitigation
End-to-end VLSI design framework for CFET technology
Elimination of design rule violations (DRVs) while maintaining area advantages

metrics.other: DRV elimination with maintained area advantages

primary_theme: Routability solutions for CFET-based VLSI at sub-5nm scales
